items.title: Nvidia revenue doubles to $115.8B and guides to $130B
items.summary: In its first report since Jensen Huang's exit, Nvidia's Q3 revenue rose 103% from a year ago, with data center sales of $107.6 billion, and it guided Q4 revenue to about $130 billion excluding China. AI chip demand is still accelerating despite the leadership turmoil.

items.title: California attorney general subpoenas Nvidia over China and disclosures
items.summary: California's AG served Nvidia with an investigative subpoena to learn whether its chips or confidential data reached China and whether it misled investors, adding to class actions and other probes. It raises legal and regulatory risk, though it is not a finding of wrongdoing.

items.title: Nvidia board rules out bringing Huang back as CEO
items.summary: Nvidia's board said it does not plan to reinstate founder Jensen Huang and is moving ahead with a search for a permanent CEO. That settles one question but leaves the company without its long-time leader for an extended stretch.

items.title: US rule curbs remote access to advanced AI chips abroad
items.summary: The Commerce Department issued an interim rule to stop China and others from reaching restricted AI chips through data centers in third countries. It adds compliance burdens and could trim some overseas data center demand for top AI accelerators.

items.title: Anthropic IPO puts a big value on Google's stake
items.summary: Anthropic listed on Nasdaq in a record IPO, and Google will hold about 13.4% of the AI lab in non-voting shares. The listing turns Alphabet's early bet into a large, now publicly priced asset alongside its cloud partnership.
